prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1370; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a side impact at an intersection and stated the other vehicle entered from the left while the claimant had the green light. The claimant reports a concussion and is not represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Reviewed the scene photos and the vehicle damage, which are mostly in line with the described impact. The claimant's account has been consistent so far.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the collision happened as the claimant described. Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the sequence of events.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.

Entry 5: Claimant has been asked where they were seated at impact, and the answer is still unclear. The seating position will need to be clarified before the injury analysis is finalized.

Entry 6: Claimant provided a few additional details on a follow-up call. The core account of the crash remained the same as the first report.

Entry 7: Medical records show the concussion treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 8: It is not yet clear whether the concussion was caused by this crash, so the injury portion stays open pending further medical review. The property damage portion is being processed on its own track.
